summary: Exhaustively find the NATIVE (config-only) DRBD-9 way to get split-brain-free incremental heal on quorum-loss failover, before any kernel patch

final.why_it_works:
The earlier "must patch" conclusion rested on the premise that the loser's UUID rotation forces a FULL resync or a hard, operator-only split-brain on heal. The 9.3.2 source (HEAD a46cbd9, verified directly) shows that is false for scenario B, but ALSO that the synthesis's looser phrasing ("heals to AUTO_RECOVER") needed the verification's correction: nothing heals automatically until after-sb is set.

Mechanism: both sides rotate current-UUID from common ancestor C0. rotate_current_into_bitmap stores the OLD current (C0) into peer_md[node].bitmap_uuid (drbd_main.c:4875/4900), so C0 lands in the BITMAP slot of both sides, not history. On heal, drbd_uuid_compare reaches RULE_BITMAP_BOTH (drbd_receiver.c:4888-4892): self==peer==C0, C0!=0 -> returns SPLIT_BRAIN_AUTO_RECOVER (SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT at :4907 only fires if the ancestor were solely in HISTORY). need_full_sync_after_split_brain = (strategy == SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT) is evaluated at drbd_receiver.c:5404 BEFORE remap, so it is FALSE for AUTO_RECOVER; the full-sync promotion at :5434-5441 is skipped and the USE_BITMAP result stays incremental (SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP's .full_sync_equivalent is the distinct full-sync SYNC_TARGET_SET_BITMAP, drbd_receiver.c:189-194).

But AUTO_RECOVER only enters the recover block (drbd_receiver.c:5406) and, if still split-brain, calls drbd_asb_recover_Np. With after-sb-0pri=discard-zero-changes the zero-write loser (ch_self==0) maps to SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP (drbd_receiver.c:4330-4332); its out-of-sync bitmap toward the survivor is ~empty (it wrote nothing under suspend-io), so the "incremental" resync moves essentially zero blocks — no StandAlone, no --discard-my-data. That is the native solution. I additionally confirmed a live-quorum shortcut at drbd_receiver.c:5410-5416 that, when quorum states DISAGREE at the handshake instant and pro_version>=113, maps directly to SYNC_{SOURCE,TARGET}_USE_BITMAP before after-sb even runs — a bonus path, but it usually does NOT fire because the loser has regained quorum by heal, which is exactly why after-sb must be configured rather than relied on implicitly.

Layer 2 is mechanistically cleaner: a self-outdated loser fails drbd_data_accessible(NEW) (drbd_state.c:6384, true only for D_UP_TO_DATE) so the create_new_uuid arm at drbd_state.c:3096-3099 never sets; the loser never rotates; self==peer survives to heal; the purpose-built RULE_LOST_QUORUM branch (drbd_receiver.c:4785-4798, keyed on UUID_FLAG_PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM, reachable only inside the self==peer block at :4742) returns a directional IF_BOTH_FAILED resync resolved by disk states with zero diverged data. This is the path LINBIT designed for quorum-loss failover.
final.fencing_role: OPTIONAL belt-and-suspenders (Layer 2) and the LINBIT field standard; NOT required for the goal because Layer 1 already heals incrementally. Its value is to prevent the loser rotation entirely, yielding a zero-resync heal instead of a near-empty USE_BITMAP resync. An OUTDATED disk fails drbd_data_accessible (drbd_state.c:6384) and an OUTDATED peer is excluded by lost_contact_to_peer_data (drbd_state.c:3749-3750), so the unguarded create_new_uuid arm (drbd_state.c:3096-3099) never fires. CRITICAL asymmetry confirmed in source: native DRBD fencing only outdates the PEER from the SURVIVOR side (conn_try_outdate_peer via the fence-peer khelper, drbd_state.c:3799-3816 / drbd_nl.c:840-874) — there is NO autonomous in-kernel trigger for the MINORITY loser to self-outdate under a hard partition. All four __outdate_myself call sites are inside 2PC handlers requiring connectivity (drbd_state.c:5854, :6084; drbd_receiver.c:6961, :7237), and quorum loss alone only sets susp_io, never D_OUTDATED. Therefore fencing helps ONLY if bedrock-d (which already detects the minority) issues `drbdadm outdate <res>` on its OWN local resource. Use `fencing resource-only` (handler-driven), NOT resource-and-stonith, to keep STONITH/reboot ownership with bedrock-d.
final.after_sb_role: LOAD-BEARING and the single most important fix — the original config never set it, which is the WHOLE reason the operator saw StandAlone + --discard-my-data. Verification refined the synthesis here: AUTO_RECOVER is not self-healing (.disconnect=true); with everything at the default ASB_DISCONNECT, the recover functions return SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT and the link drops to StandAlone. Setting after-sb-0pri=discard-zero-changes makes the zero-write loser the incremental SYNC_TARGET when both nodes are Secondary at heal (pcount==0; ch_self==0 -> SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP, drbd_receiver.c:4330-4332). after-sb-1pri=discard-secondary covers the pcount==1 window where the ex-Primary is still R_PRIMARY at the handshake instant (discard-zero-changes is a "Configuration error" there, drbd_receiver.c:4378-4381): ASB_DISCARD_SECONDARY returns SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP for a Secondary and SYNC_SOURCE_USE_BITMAP for a Primary (drbd_receiver.c:4396) — so it is correct ONLY paired with on-suspended-primary-outdated force-secondary, which demotes the ex-Primary so the loser is Secondary; otherwise discard-secondary would wrongly make the loser the SyncSource and overwrite the survivor. after-sb-2pri MUST stay disconnect so a genuine dual-WRITE two-primary brain still hard-stops (drbd_asb_recover_2p, drbd_receiver.c:4449-4450). Net policy: discard-zero-changes / discard-secondary / disconnect + force-secondary deterministically resolves scenario B to an incremental, correct-direction resync with no operator action.
final.bedrock_d_operations: 1) Remain the SOLE promote authority (auto-promote OFF): promote the new Primary ONLY on the majority side after the witness/election verdict; never let DRBD self-promote. 2) On detecting the LOCAL node is in the minority (which bedrock-d already does), run `drbdadm outdate <res>` on the local resource immediately (Layer 2), or drive it via the fence-peer handler reading the witness verdict — BEFORE the heal handshake — so the loser never rotates current-UUID. DRBD cannot self-outdate the loser under a hard partition, so bedrock-d MUST drive it. 3) Roll out the after-sb policies (Layer 1) UNIFORMLY into the resource template on all 3-5 nodes (any mismatch => hard connection refusal, drbd_receiver.c:5625-5638) for both the arbiter "cluster" resource and every VM-disk resource. 4) Keep on-suspended-primary-outdated force-secondary (already set) so the returning ex-Primary demotes and reintegrates as SyncTarget. 5) Order the failover: promote the majority-side Primary and outdate/demote the minority loser promptly within the failover window, so the heal handshake sees the loser as Secondary/Outdated. 6) No kernel patch needed for v1.0; the patch is a deferred hardening item only.
final.residual_risks: (a) Quorum-override timing (drbd_receiver.c:5410-5416): the live-quorum shortcut only fires if quorum states DISAGREE at the handshake instant and pro_version>=113; on heal the loser has usually regained quorum, so this branch typically does NOT fire and the after-sb policy is what saves it — hence after-sb must be explicitly configured, not relied on implicitly. (b) Role at heal: if the ex-Primary is still R_PRIMARY at the handshake (force-secondary via the diverged-UUID reconnect path may not fire because peer_data_is_successor_of_mine can return false when both rotated), pcount==1 and after-sb-1pri governs; discard-secondary is correct only because force-secondary demotes the ex-Primary — VERIFY on the testbed that the loser resolves to SYNC_TARGET before trusting it, else a misfire could make the loser SyncSource and overwrite the survivor. (c) Non-zero-write loser: if the loser admitted even one write between quorum-loss detection and freeze, discard-zero-changes sees ch_self>0 and falls through to discard-least-changes (which can pick the wrong side); with quorum suspend-io and zero in-flight this should not happen, but confirm. (d) Layer-2 outdate must win the race against the create_new_uuid arm in a PARTIAL partition; if the outdate lands after the arm, the loser still rotates — but that just drops back to the (still-safe) Layer-1 path. (e) after-sb policies are DATA-DISCARDING by nature; they are safe here ONLY because bedrock-d guarantees the discarded (minority) side wrote nothing and is the correct loser. Worst case: never a silent overwrite of the survivor — either a clean incremental resync of the empty loser, or (a genuine dual-write brain) a hard StandAlone caught by after-sb-2pri disconnect that requires operator action.
final.patch_still_needed: no — not for the stated GOAL on v1.0. The unguarded UUID rotation is real and not preventable by any quorum config option (the create_new_uuid arm at drbd_state.c:3096-3099 and execute at :4466-4471 ignore have_quorum even though it is in scope), but the native after-sb config already delivers incremental, split-brain-free, no-operator heal for the observed scenario, and the bedrock-d local-outdate handler delivers the zero-resync form. A kernel guard (gate the arm/execute on !PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM / have_quorum[NEW], mirroring the existing guards at drbd_sender.c:3443 and drbd_receiver.c:9886) is a defensible v1.x HARDENING: it would (i) turn the heal into a true zero-resync RULE_LOST_QUORUM reintegration and (ii) defend the rare non-zero-write residual case (c) and remove the timing/role dependencies of residual risks (a)/(b)/(d) without relying on bedrock-d outdate timing. Residual case it would cover that config cannot fully guarantee: a loser that wrote >0 blocks in the window between quorum-loss detection and IO freeze AND reconnects while still R_PRIMARY — config mitigates but does not provably eliminate this corner. Not a v1.0 blocker.
load_bearing_claims: VERIFIED in source: SPLIT_BRAIN_AUTO_RECOVER does NOT auto-heal by itself — its descriptor has .disconnect=true (drbd_receiver.c:209-211, confirmed). It only routes into drbd_asb_recover_{0,1,2}p; under default after-sb=ASB_DISCONNECT those return SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT -> StandAlone. So the after-sb config is THE fix, not optional polish. (This corrects the synthesis's loose 'heals to AUTO_RECOVER' wording flagged by verification.)

VERIFIED: scenario B reaches RULE_BITMAP_BOTH and returns SPLIT_BRAIN_AUTO_RECOVER when both bitmap_uuids == common ancestor !=0 (drbd_receiver.c:4888-4892); DISCONNECT (:4907) only if the ancestor is solely in HISTORY.

VERIFIED: need_full_sync_after_split_brain = (strategy==SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT) at drbd_receiver.c:5404 is evaluated before remap, FALSE for AUTO_RECOVER, so the full-sync promotion at :5434-5441 is skipped; USE_BITMAP stays incremental.

VERIFIED: a live-quorum override exists at drbd_receiver.c:5410-5416 mapping disagreeing-quorum heals directly to SYNC_{SOURCE,TARGET}_USE_BITMAP before after-sb runs — but it typically does NOT fire on heal (loser regained quorum), so after-sb is the operative lever.
VERIFIED: SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP (.full_sync_equivalent = SYNC_TARGET_SET_BITMAP) is a distinct incremental strategy from the full-sync SET_BITMAP (drbd_receiver.c:189-200).
after-sb-0pri discard-zero-changes maps a zero-write side to SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP (drbd_receiver.c:4330-4332); 'Configuration error' in 1pri (:4378-4381) — confirmed by verification.
after-sb-1pri discard-secondary maps a Secondary to SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP (drbd_receiver.c:4396); correct ONLY if the loser is Secondary, which force-secondary ensures — confirmed.
after-sb-2pri disconnect hard-stops a genuine dual-write brain (drbd_receiver.c:4449-4450) — confirmed; no silent overwrite possible.
after-sb-* must be identical cluster-wide or the P_PROTOCOL handshake refuses with CS_HARD (drbd_receiver.c:5625-5638) — confirmed.

The loser's UUID rotation is genuinely unguarded by any quorum config option; arm at drbd_state.c:3096-3099, execute at :4466-4471 ignore have_quorum despite it being in scope — confirmed. Preventable only by outdating the local disk or a kernel patch.
Self-outdating the loser suppresses rotation: an outdated disk fails drbd_data_accessible (drbd_state.c:6384) so create_new_uuid is never armed — confirmed.

DRBD has NO autonomous trigger for the minority loser to self-outdate under a hard partition; all four __outdate_myself sites are 2PC/connectivity-gated (drbd_state.c:5854,:6084; drbd_receiver.c:6961,:7237) — confirmed. bedrock-d MUST drive the local outdate.
RULE_LOST_QUORUM (zero-resync clean path) is reachable only inside the self==peer block (drbd_receiver.c:4742, :4785-4798), i.e. only if the loser did NOT rotate — confirmed.

Source pinned at 9.3.2 HEAD a46cbd9, matching Bedrock's installed kmod-drbd9x-9.3.2 (build-iso.sh / MANIFEST); the ChangeLog 9.2.18 fix is DISKLESS-primary only and does not cover the diskful frozen-Primary path — confirmed.
Option spellings verified in headers: on_susp_primary_outdated is a real resource option (drbd_genl.h:152); on-no-quorum defaults to ONQ_SUSPEND_IO (drbd_limits.h:321).

verdicts.claim: Scenario B heals to SPLIT_BRAIN_AUTO_RECOVER, not SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT: drbd_receiver.c:4888-4892 (RULE_BITMAP_BOTH) returns SPLIT_BRAIN_AUTO_RECOVER when both sides' bitmap_uuid == common ancestor and != 0; DISCONNECT (:4907) only if the ancestor is solely in HISTORY.
verdicts.evidence:
The CODE CITATIONS are verbatim-correct, but the word "heals" is misleading: under default config BOTH enums drop the connection.

(1) Lines confirmed exactly — /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_receiver.c:4888-4892:
  "*rule = RULE_BITMAP_BOTH;
   self = bitmap_uuid & ~UUID_PRIMARY;
   peer = peer_device->bitmap_uuids[node_id] & ~UUID_PRIMARY;
   if (self == peer && self != ((u64)0))
       return SPLIT_BRAIN_AUTO_RECOVER;"
And :4894-4908 (RULE_HISTORY_BOTH) loops over history_uuids and "if (self == peer) return SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT;" at :4907 — only reached after the bitmap-both check at :4892 fell through. So the DISCONNECT-via-:4907 path does require the common ancestor to be found in HISTORY. Accurate.

(2) BUT "heals to AUTO_RECOVER" implies automatic recovery. REFUTED for default config. The descriptor table (drbd_receiver.c:207-216) gives BOTH enums '.is_split_brain = true' AND '.disconnect = true':
  "[SPLIT_BRAIN_AUTO_RECOVER] = { .name = \"split-brain-auto-recover\", .is_split_brain = true, .disconnect = true, },
   [SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT]   = { .name = \"split-brain-disconnect\",   .is_split_brain = true, .disconnect = true, },"
AUTO_RECOVER only routes into drbd_asb_recover_{0,1,2}p() (drbd_receiver.c:5234-5251 / 5406-5444). Each of those functions (drbd_receiver.c:4270,4361,4423) starts 'rv = SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT' and for 'case ASB_DISCONNECT: break;' returns SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT. The DEFAULT policy is ASB_DISCONNECT — drbd-headers/linux/drbd_limits.h:158-160: "#define DRBD_AFTER_SB_0P_DEF ASB_DISCONNECT / _1P_DEF ASB_DISCONNECT / _2P_DEF ASB_DISCONNECT". So under default config AUTO_RECOVER -> recover-block -> ASB_DISCONNECT -> SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT -> drbd_receiver.c:5461-5465 "Split-Brain detected but unresolved, dropping connection!". The link drops either way.

(3) Official prose agrees the default does NOT auto-heal. drbd.conf-9.0 manpage (manpages.debian.org): after-sb-0pri/1pri/2pri 'disconnect' = "No automatic resynchronization; simply disconnect." DRBD 9.0 User Guide (linbit.com/drbd-user-guide/drbd-guide-9_0-en/): "DRBD does not automatically recover split brain by default ... the recommended course of action ... is to manually resolve the split brain." drbd-user list guidance: "leave the split brain recovery settings at their defaults (disconnect)".

(4) The REAL, narrower distinction (so the claim is not flatly false): SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT only consults after-sb-* when 'always_asbp' is set and forces a FULL sync (need_full_sync_after_split_brain, drbd_receiver.c:5232/5404), whereas SPLIT_BRAIN_AUTO_RECOVER always consults after-sb-* and permits a bitmap/partial resync. So the two enums differ in resync eligibility/type when after-sb-* IS configured — but NOT in "heals automatically." Verdict PLAUSIBLE: code line-references exact; the implied auto-healing semantics are false under default (disconnect) config. Both clones identical (diff -q = IDENTICAL), REL_VERSION 9.3.2 head a46cbd9.

verdicts.claim: old current UUID goes into peer bitmap_uuid slot
verdicts.evidence: DRBD 9.3.2 drbd_main.c: lines 4875/4900 store old current_uuid (set 4849-52, before new at 4964-66) into absent/weak peer bitmap slots; receiver 4892 RULE_BITMAP_BOTH=AUTO_RECOVER vs 4907 RULE_HISTORY_BOTH=DISCONNECT.

verdicts.claim: AUTO_RECOVER does NOT force a full resync: need_full_sync_after_split_brain = (strategy == SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT) is evaluated BEFORE remap (drbd_receiver.c:5404 connect path / :5232 attach path), so it is FALSE for AUTO_RECOVER and the full_sync promotion at 5434-5442 is skipped; the after-sb USE_BITMAP result stays incremental.

SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP is an incremental strategy distinct from the full-sync SYNC_TARGET_SET_BITMAP; descriptor table drbd_receiver.c:189-194 lists full_sync_equivalent=SYNC_TARGET_SET_BITMAP for USE_BITMAP.
verdicts.evidence: Descriptor table is exact, byte-identical in both clones (md5 5ee20af14b38e00b2d9b94f790f7e7ba, HEAD a46cbd9, REL_VERSION 9.3.2) and matches upstream LINBIT/drbd master. /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_receiver.c:189-194: "[SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP] = { .name = \"target-use-bitmap\", .is_sync_target = true, .full_sync_equivalent = SYNC_TARGET_SET_BITMAP, .resync_peer_preference = 3, .reverse = SYNC_SOURCE_USE_BITMAP, };". The SET_BITMAP entry at :196-201 has NO full_sync_equivalent (it is itself the full-sync strategy). The two strategies are distinct enum values (drbd_receiver.c:128-129). Incremental-vs-full distinction is proven by behavior in bitmap_mod_after_handshake (drbd_receiver.c:4966-5044): USE_BITMAP has ZERO branches (grep count 0) so it never touches/sets the bitmap and resyncs only already-dirty bits = incremental; SET_BITMAP branch at :5005-5021 runs drbd_bmio_set_allocated_n_write/drbd_bmio_set_n_write and logs (:5015) \"Setting and writing the whole bitmap, fresh node\" = full sync. The full_sync_equivalent field is actively consumed at :5258-5265 and :5435-5441 to escalate USE_BITMAP to SET_BITMAP, logging (:5264) \"Doing a full sync since UUIDs were ambiguous.\" and (:5265) \"strategy = strategy_descriptor(strategy).full_sync_equivalent;\". LINBIT user-guide/manpage prose corroborates: \"a partial (bit-map based) resync is sufficient ... more efficient than a full resync\" and \"keeping al-updates enabled (the default) allows for incremental bitmap-based resync\" vs full resync. Only quibble: the table does not merely \"list\" the field — the kernel uses it to convert the incremental strategy into a full sync — which strengthens, not refutes, the claim.

verdicts.claim: Default after-sb = ASB_DISCONNECT is the sole reason the operator saw StandAlone: drbd_asb_recover_0p/1p/2p hit `case ASB_DISCONNECT: break` and return SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT (cited :4296-4297, :4383-4384, :4449-4450).
verdicts.evidence:
VERDICT: CONFIRMED, with one filename correction — the functions live in drbd_receiver.c, NOT drbd_state.c as the claim states. The cited LINE numbers (4296-4297, 4383-4384, 4449-4450) are exactly correct for drbd_receiver.c (REL_VERSION 9.3.2, HEAD a46cbd9). Both source trees agree byte-for-byte in this region.

(1) ASB_DISCONNECT IS the default. /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd-headers/linux/drbd_limits.h:158-160:
  "#define DRBD_AFTER_SB_0P_DEF ASB_DISCONNECT
   #define DRBD_AFTER_SB_1P_DEF ASB_DISCONNECT
   #define DRBD_AFTER_SB_2P_DEF ASB_DISCONNECT"
and drbd-headers/linux/drbd_genl.h:173-175 binds these as the field defaults (after_sb_0p/1p/2p, def 0 -> *_DEF). LINBIT drbd.conf docs confirm in prose: "The default is to disconnect."

(2) The break -> SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT mechanism is exactly as described. drbd_receiver.c:
  - 0p: line 4274 "enum sync_strategy rv = SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT;" then 4296-4297 "case ASB_DISCONNECT:\n\t\tbreak;" -> returns rv (4355) unchanged = SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT.
  - 1p: line 4366 "...rv = SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT;" then 4383-4384 "case ASB_DISCONNECT:\n\t\tbreak;" -> returns SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT.
  - 2p: line 4427 "...rv = SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT;" then 4449-4450 "case ASB_DISCONNECT:\n\t\tbreak;" -> returns SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT.

(3) SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT -> StandAlone is real. sync_descriptors[SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT] at drbd_receiver.c:212-216 has ".is_split_brain = true, .disconnect = true". In drbd_sync_handshake the unresolved split-brain returns this strategy (drbd_receiver.c:5461-5464 "Split-Brain detected but unresolved, dropping connection!" + khelper "split-brain"); the caller receive_state takes the .disconnect path (8346) and for the classic case "goto fail" -> drbd_receiver.c:8516-8518 "fail:\n\tchange_cstate(connection, C_DISCONNECTING, CS_HARD);". conn_disconnect then promotes that to StandAlone: drbd_receiver.c:10144-10146 "if (oc == C_DISCONNECTING)\n\t\tchange_cstate_tag(connection, C_STANDALONE, ...". LINBIT User Guide confirms in prose: "After split brain has been detected, one node will always have the resource in a StandAlone connection state" and for after-sb-0pri default "disconnect ... No automatic resynchronisation, simply disconnect" (linbit.com/drbd-user-guide/drbd-guide-9_0-en/, drbd.conf-9.0 manpage).

CAVEAT on the word "sole": confirmed as the cause of THIS unresolved-split-brain StandAlone. But StandAlone is also reachable by other independent paths (e.g. drbd_receiver.c:1030 "no-dest-addr", manual drbdadm disconnect, protocol/auth failure). The claim is sound only insofar as the operator's event was an after-split-brain StandAlone; if so, the default ASB_DISCONNECT is indeed why no auto-recovery happened and the connection dropped to StandAlone. The ChangeLog 9.3.2 note "Handle split-brain recovery strategies during attach" added the attach-time variant (drbd_receiver.c:5270-5274) but did not change the default-disconnect behavior.

verdicts.claim: after-sb-0pri discard-zero-changes maps a zero-write side to SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP: drbd_receiver.c:4330-4332 (ch_self==0 -> SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP); valid only for pcount==0 (it is a 'Configuration error' in 1pri at :4378-4381).
verdicts.evidence:
All three sub-claims verified against LINBIT/drbd 9.3.2 (HEAD a46cbd9), and both clones (/tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_receiver.c and /home/tommy/projects/drbdsrc_clone/drbd/drbd_receiver.c are byte-identical: `diff -q` = IDENTICAL).

(1) EXACT LINE MATCH for the zero-write->target mapping. In drbd_asb_recover_0p(), case ASB_DISCARD_ZERO_CHG, drbd_receiver.c:4330-4332:
  4330  `\t\t\tif (ch_self == 0) {`
  4331  `\t\t\t\trv = SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP;`
  4332  `\t\t\t\tbreak;`
ch_self is the LOCAL node's changed-block count: drbd_receiver.c:4282 `ch_self = peer_device->comm_bm_set;`, and drbd_int.h:1456 documents `unsigned long comm_bm_set; /* communicated number of set bits. */` (out-of-sync blocks the local node wrote). So ch_self==0 = local side wrote zero blocks -> local node becomes the sync TARGET. SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP has `.is_sync_target = true` (drbd_receiver.c:189-191 in the sync_descriptors table), i.e. the target's data is overwritten/discarded. (Symmetric peer-zero case is ch_peer==0 -> SYNC_SOURCE_USE_BITMAP at 4326-4328.)

(2) This handler is reached ONLY for pcount==0. drbd_receiver.c:5236-5250: `int pcount = (device->resource->role[NOW] == R_PRIMARY) + (peer_role == R_PRIMARY); ... switch (pcount) { case 0: strategy = drbd_asb_recover_0p(peer_device); break; case 1: ...recover_1p... case 2: ...recover_2p... }`. The function header at drbd_receiver.c:4268 confirms: `drbd_asb_recover_0p - Recover after split-brain with no remaining primaries`.

(3) EXACT LINE MATCH for the 1pri 'Configuration error'. In drbd_asb_recover_1p(), drbd_receiver.c:4378-4382:
  4378  `\tcase ASB_DISCARD_ZERO_CHG:`
  4379  `\tcase ASB_RETRY_CONNECT:`
  4380  `\tcase ASB_AUTO_DISCARD:`
  4381  `\t\tdrbd_err(device, \"Configuration error.\\n\");`
  4382  `\t\tbreak;`
So with one remaining primary, discard-zero-changes is rejected as a config error, exactly as claimed.

Enum identity: drbd-headers/linux/drbd.h:56 `ASB_DISCARD_ZERO_CHG,` in enum drbd_after_sb_p; adjacency to ASB_DISCARD_LEAST_CHG is cross-checked by the in-tree warning string at drbd_receiver.c:4318 ("Using discard-least-changes instead").

Official prose corroboration (drbd.conf-9.0 manpage, manpages.debian.org): after-sb-0pri 'discard-zero-changes' = "If only one of the nodes wrote data since the split brain situation was detected, resynchronize from this node to the other. If both nodes wrote data, disconnect." The node that wrote nothing is the resync target (its data discarded) -> matches ch_self==0 -> SYNC_TARGET_USE_BITMAP. The same manpage lists after-sb-1pri valid policies as disconnect/consensus/violently-as0p/discard-secondary/call-pri-lost-after-sb only — discard-zero-changes is NOT among them, matching the 'Configuration error' at :4381.

Minor framing note (does not refute): the cited :4378-4381 range is a fall-through group of cases 4373-4380 all landing on the single drbd_err at 4381; the claim's bracket correctly spans ASB_DISCARD_ZERO_CHG (4378) through the error line (4381).

after-sb-2pri disconnect still hard-stops a genuine dual-write brain: drbd_asb_recover_2p :4449-4450 returns SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT.
verdicts.evidence:
TECHNICAL SUBSTANCE CONFIRMED; one citation error (wrong file). The function is in drbd_receiver.c, NOT drbd_state.c as the claim states (grep: "asb_recover... NONE in drbd_state.c"; drbd_state.c:4449-4450 is unrelated `send_new_state_to_all_peer_devices`). But the LINE NUMBERS are right for drbd_receiver.c. [LINBIT/drbd 9.3.2, HEAD a46cbd9]

(1) The function and its default-policy branch — /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_receiver.c:4423-4450:
"4423  static enum sync_strategy drbd_asb_recover_2p(struct drbd_peer_device *peer_device)
4427    enum sync_strategy strategy, rv = SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT;   // rv initialized to DISCONNECT
4431    after_sb_2p = rcu_dereference(...)->after_sb_2p;
4433    switch (after_sb_2p) {
4449      case ASB_DISCONNECT:
4450        break;            // rv stays SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT
4471    return rv;"
So under the disconnect policy the function returns SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT exactly as claimed (line 4449=`case ASB_DISCONNECT:`, 4450=`break;`).

(2) It is the DEFAULT — drbd-headers/linux/drbd_limits.h:160: "#define DRBD_AFTER_SB_2P_DEF ASB_DISCONNECT" (and drbd_genl.h:175 ties after_sb_2p to DRBD_AFTER_SB_2P_DEF).

(3) "genuine dual-write brain": SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT is returned by drbd_uuid_compare at receiver.c:4907 under RULE_HISTORY_BOTH — current UUIDs differ AND a common ancestor sits in BOTH histories (both sides wrote new data since divergence). The milder same-bitmap case returns SPLIT_BRAIN_AUTO_RECOVER (4892). So DISCONNECT == true divergence.

(4) "hard-stops": SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT descriptor has `.disconnect = true` (receiver.c:212-216). At receiver.c:5461-5465 the handshake logs "Split-Brain detected but unresolved, dropping connection!" and returns it; the dispatcher at receiver.c:8346 `else if (strategy_descriptor(strategy).disconnect)` then sets CONN_HANDSHAKE_DISCONNECT / goto fail — connection dropped, NO resync. Note the recover_2p fn is only invoked when always_asbp is set (5235/5406); with the bare default it never runs and the strategy short-circuits to the same drop at 5461 — either way: hard-stop.

(5) Official corroboration — drbd.conf-9.0 manpage (manpages.debian.org/.../drbd.conf-9.0.5): after-sb-2pri "disconnect" = "No automatic resynchronization, simply disconnect." DRBD 9.0 User Guide: no automatic policy is safe when both nodes were primary; manual intervention required. drbdsetup-9.0 confirms `disconnect` is the documented default for after-sb-2pri.

VERDICT: claim's behavioral assertion is fully correct (default after-sb-2pri=disconnect returns SPLIT_BRAIN_DISCONNECT and drops the connection on genuine dual-write divergence). The only defect is the file attribution: it says drbd_state.c but the code is in drbd_receiver.c (the :4449-4450 line numbers happen to match receiver.c; drbd_state.c:4466 is the unrelated UUID-rotation code from a different lesson note, the likely source of the mix-up).

verdicts.claim: after-sb settings must be identical cluster-wide or the connection is refused: drbd_receiver.c:5625-5638 ('incompatible after-sb-0pri/1pri/2pri settings').

The loser's UUID rotation is genuinely unguarded by quorum: the arm at drbd_state.c:3096-3099 checks only role==R_PRIMARY && drbd_data_accessible(NEW); the execute at :4466-4471 checks only (!susp_uuid[OLD] && susp_uuid[NEW] && NEW_CUR_UUID) with have_quorum[NEW] in scope (used at :4463) but not consulted — confirming the rotation is not preventable by any quorum config option, only by outdating or a kernel guard.

(1) ARM — drbd_state.c:3096-3099: "if (lost_contact_to_peer_data(peer_disk_state)) { / if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && !test_bit(UNREGISTERED, &device->flags) && / drbd_data_accessible(device, NEW)) / create_new_uuid = true;". (The claim omits the !UNREGISTERED check but its point — no quorum gate — holds.) drbd_data_accessible (drbd_state.c:6379-6385) returns true whenever the local disk is D_UP_TO_DATE, independent of quorum — so a frozen quorum-lost Primary satisfies it.

Promoted __NEW_CUR_UUID->NEW_CUR_UUID at :906-908. susp_uuid[NEW] flips true at :2476-2483 on a suspend->unsuspend edge while NEW_CUR_UUID is set.

(3) EXECUTE — drbd_state.c:4466-4471: "if (!susp_uuid[OLD] && susp_uuid[NEW] && / test_and_clear_bit(NEW_CUR_UUID, &device->flags)) / new_current_uuid = true; / if (new_current_uuid) / drbd_uuid_new_current(device, false);". Exactly the (!susp_uuid[OLD] && susp_uuid[NEW] && NEW_CUR_UUID) triple in the claim; no quorum term.

(4) have_quorum IS in scope but NOT consulted: declared at :3963 "bool *have_quorum = device_state_change->have_quorum;" inside the same n_device loop; referenced only at :4226 and :4463 ("if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && have_quorum[OLD] && !have_quorum[NEW]) drbd_maybe_khelper(... 'quorum-lost')") — three lines above the execute — and is absent from 4466-4471. Claim's "in scope, used at :4463, not consulted at execute" is exact.

(5) The execute function carries no internal guard: drbd_uuid_new_current (drbd_main.c:5273-5303) checks only get_ldev_if_state(D_UP_TO_DATE) and peer-need predicates — no quorum/suspend check.

(6) A quorum guard is available and idiomatic but deliberately omitted here: at drbd_state.c:2885-2886, in the SAME finish_state_change pass, "if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && !have_quorum[NEW]) set_bit(PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM, &device->flags)" — the kernel already knows quorum is lost. The write route (drbd_sender.c:3443 "if (device->have_quorum[NOW] && drbd_data_accessible(...))") and the disconnect route (drbd_receiver.c:9886 "!test_bit(PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM, &device->flags)") both DO consult quorum; the susp_uuid execute path does not. So a guard is preventable only by a kernel patch, not by the absent path itself.

(7) No config option prevents it: drbd.conf-9.0(5) (manpages.debian.org) — quorum, on-no-quorum, quorum-minimum-redundancy, on-suspended-primary-outdated each govern only promotion eligibility / IO error-vs-freeze / demotion; "None of these options mention UUID rotation or generation identifier creation." on-suspended-primary-outdated SPO_FORCE_SECONDARY is consulted only in the reconnect/handshake path (drbd_receiver.c:843, :914, :8095), never in the arm/execute, so it fires AFTER any rotation. This confirms 'not preventable by any quorum config option.' The only remaining preventers are outdating the local disk (which makes drbd_data_accessible(NEW) false, disarming the arm) or a kernel guard — exactly as claimed.

Every refutation angle (config options, internal-function guard, alternate paths, have_quorum scope, suspend-state gating) was checked and each supports the claim. Note: the cited line numbers are exact against HEAD a46cbd9; they would shift in other revisions.

verdicts.claim: An OUTDATED loser suppresses the rotation: lost_contact_to_peer_data excludes D_OUTDATED peers (drbd_state.c:3749-3750) and drbd_data_accessible returns true only for D_UP_TO_DATE local/peer (drbd_state.c:6384, :6393) — so a self-outdated loser never arms create_new_uuid.
verdicts.evidence:
Both cited code facts match the pinned source EXACTLY (LINBIT/drbd 9.3.2, HEAD a46cbd9; /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd == /home/tommy/projects/drbdsrc_clone/drbd, byte-identical).

(1) lost_contact_to_peer_data excludes D_OUTDATED peers — drbd_state.c:3744-3751:
  "static bool lost_contact_to_peer_data(enum drbd_disk_state *peer_disk_state) {
     enum drbd_disk_state os = peer_disk_state[OLD]; ... ns = peer_disk_state[NEW];
     return (os >= D_INCONSISTENT && os != D_UNKNOWN && os != D_OUTDATED)
            && (ns < D_INCONSISTENT || ns == D_UNKNOWN || ns == D_OUTDATED); }"
The parameter is the PEER's disk-state pair. The first conjunct's "os != D_OUTDATED" means an already-OUTDATED peer yields false. (Note: this gate is about the PEER being outdated, not self.)

(2) drbd_data_accessible true only for D_UP_TO_DATE — drbd_state.c:6379-6401:
  ":6384  if (device->disk_state[which] == D_UP_TO_DATE) return true;"
  ":6393  if (peer_device->disk_state[which] == D_UP_TO_DATE) { data_accessible = true; break; }"
  then ":6400 return data_accessible;" (i.e. false). Returns true iff local OR some allow_remote_read peer is D_UP_TO_DATE.

The conjunction that gates rotation — drbd_state.c:3096-3099 (inside after_state_ch):
  "if (lost_contact_to_peer_data(peer_disk_state)) {
     if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && !test_bit(UNREGISTERED, &device->flags) && drbd_data_accessible(device, NEW))
        create_new_uuid = true; ...}"
For a SELF-outdated loser the operative suppressor is drbd_data_accessible(device, NEW)==false: a self-outdated node is not D_UP_TO_DATE (enum order drbd.h:248: D_OUTDATED=6 < D_UP_TO_DATE=9) and, having lost its up-to-date peer, has no D_UP_TO_DATE peer either, so :6384/:6393 both fail. Then create_new_uuid stays false and the arming bit at :3135-3136 "if (create_new_uuid && !susp_uuid[OLD]) set_bit(__NEW_CUR_UUID,...)" is never set.

"never" holds across ALL eight create_new_uuid/arming paths in this function: every one requires role[NEW]==R_PRIMARY with drbd_data_accessible (:3098,:3113,:3128), or disk_state[NEW]==D_UP_TO_DATE (:3108), or Secondary->Primary promotion (:3132), or L_AHEAD entry (:3094) — none reachable by a self-outdated, data-inaccessible node.

The loser also cannot sneak in as Primary-with-fresh-peer: sanitize_state drbd_state.c:1740-1747 sets "any_disk_up_to_date[which] = drbd_data_accessible(device, which)" and "if (!(role[OLD]==R_PRIMARY && !any_disk_up_to_date[OLD]) && (role[NEW]==R_PRIMARY && !any_disk_up_to_date[NEW])) return SS_NO_UP_TO_DATE_DISK;". And on reconnect to a successor peer the loser is force-demoted, not kept Primary: drbd_receiver.c:8114-8117 "if (data_successor && resource->role[NOW]==R_PRIMARY) { drbd_warn(... \"Remote node has more recent data\"); maybe_force_secondary(peer_device); ...}" and :8095-8101 (SPO_FORCE_SECONDARY -> role[NEW]=R_SECONDARY). Default is SPO_DISCONNECT (drbd_limits.h:323 DRBD_ON_SUSP_PRI_OUTD_DEF SPO_DISCONNECT), i.e. it stays frozen/disconnected and never reconnect-bumps. If it does reconnect to a stable up-to-date peer it is upgraded via resync, not left outdated-primary (drbd_state.c:2316-2326 "Upgrade myself from D_OUTDATED").

Documentation agrees with the design intent. drbdsetup-9.0 on-suspended-primary-outdated (manpages.debian.org/testing/drbd-utils/drbdsetup-9.0.8.en.html) describes exactly this case — a quorum-frozen primary connects to a quorate partition where another node "started a newer data-generation" — and force-secondary "will demote to secondary immediately, and fail all pending (and new) IO requests with IO errors" (no new generation by the loser). The DRBD 9.0 User Guide generation-identifiers rule (16.x) is the inverse case: a PRIMARY with accessible data bumps UUID on losing its peer — which is precisely the path drbd_data_accessible/role[NEW]==R_PRIMARY guards.

Caveat (does not refute): the claim's wording loosely attributes the SELF-outdated suppression partly to the D_OUTDATED-peer exclusion in lost_contact_to_peer_data; that exclusion actually concerns the PEER's state, while the self-outdated suppression is carried by drbd_data_accessible (also cited). Both gates are real and both are quoted correctly, so the claim points at the correct machinery and the conclusion is sound.

verdicts.claim: DRBD has no autonomous trigger for the MINORITY loser to self-outdate under a hard partition: __outdate_myself only runs inside 2PC requiring connectivity (drbd_state.c:6083-6084, drbd_receiver.c:7235-7237); thus bedrock-d (or a fence-peer handler) must drive the local outdate.
verdicts.evidence:
CORE MECHANISM CONFIRMED (with a minor citation correction in the claim's favor). In LINBIT/drbd 9.3.2 (HEAD a46cbd9), `__outdate_myself` has EXACTLY FOUR call sites, and EVERY one is inside a two-phase-commit (2PC) handler that processes a twopc_reply/twopc_request/twopc_state_change — i.e. requires a reachable peer driving the commit. The claim cites only 3 and is slightly off on line numbers, but the missed 4th site reinforces it.

Definition: drbd_state.c:5786 `void __outdate_myself(struct drbd_resource *resource)` → loops devices and `__change_disk_state(device, D_OUTDATED)`.

The four (and only) call sites — all 2PC-gated:
1. drbd_state.c:5854 in `do_twopc_after_lost_peer()` — guarded by `if (phase == PH_COMMIT && (reply->primary_nodes & ~directly_reachable && !pri_incapable))` (5853-5854); `reply` is `&resource->twopc_reply`.
2. drbd_state.c:6084 in `do_change_cstate()` — inside `if (phase == PH_COMMIT)` (6079), `if (reply->primary_nodes & ~directly_reachable)` (6083-6084). [claim's "6083-6084"; actual call at 6084.]
3. drbd_receiver.c:6961 in `change_connection_state()` (sig at 6908-6912, "Two phase commit reply" doc 6902) — `if (reply && !abort) { ... if (reply->primary_nodes & ~directly_reachable) __outdate_myself(resource);` (6956-6961). [NOT cited by the claim.]
4. drbd_receiver.c:7237 in `far_away_change(struct drbd_connection*, struct twopc_request *request, struct twopc_reply *reply, ...)` (sig 7168-7172) — `if (state_change->primary_nodes & ~directly_reachable && !(request->flags & TWOPC_PRI_INCAPABLE)) __outdate_myself(resource);` (7235-7237). [claim's "7235-7237"; actual call at 7237.]

ATTEMPTED REFUTATIONS, ALL FAILED:
(a) Quorum loss does NOT self-outdate. drbd_state.c:2473-2474 `resource->susp_quorum[NEW] = resource->res_opts.on_no_quorum == ONQ_SUSPEND_IO ? !resource_has_quorum : false;` — losing quorum only sets I/O suspend (or io-error via ONQ_IO_ERROR at 897); the disk stays UpToDate. DRBD-9 User Guide (linbit.com/drbd-user-guide/drbd-guide-9_0-en/): "By default DRBD freezes IO on a device, that lost quorum"; "it completes all IO operations with an error if quorum is lost." No disk-state change.

(b) Hard-partition cleanup does NOT self-outdate. On link loss the receiver issues `change_cstate(connection, C_NETWORK_FAILURE/C_BROKEN_PIPE, CS_HARD)` (drbd_receiver.c:636, 935, 11480, 11645, 11668, 11712, 11724) and `conn_disconnect()` (9995) re-asserts `change_cstate_tag(connection, C_NETWORK_FAILURE, CS_HARD, ...)` (10014). The only fencing action in conn_disconnect is `if (resource->role[NOW] == R_PRIMARY && fencing_policy != FP_DONT_CARE ...) conn_try_outdate_peer_async(connection);` (10123-10126) — that outdates the PEER (fence-peer khelper), never self. Critically, the polite self-outdate path `outdate_on_disconnect()` (5971-5990, "secondary politely disconnect from primary, proposes to outdate itself") is reached ONLY via do_change_cstate at 6052 `if (context->val.conn == C_DISCONNECTING && !(context->flags & CS_HARD))` — a HARD partition produces C_NETWORK_FAILURE/C_BROKEN_PIPE with CS_HARD, so this is bypassed.

(c) The "connect failed, outdate local disks" path is handshake-mediated, not partition-autonomous. drbd_receiver.c:828 `apply_local_state_change()` comment 830-831: "Although the connect failed, outdate local disks if we learn from the handshake that the peer has more recent data" — requires a (re)handshake with the peer; under a hard partition there is no handshake.

(d) sender.c:1730 `__outdate_peer_disk_by_mask` (called at 2044 inside resync-finished, requires UUIDS_RECEIVED/active link) and drbd_nl.c:840 `conn_try_outdate_peer` (invokes the `fence-peer` khelper at 874) both outdate the PEER, and require connectivity/a userspace handler. The only local D_OUTDATED via nl is the admin `drbdadm outdate` command (drbd_nl.c:6212), i.e. operator/handler-driven.

OFFICIAL DOCS corroborate: User Guide — fence-peer "handler is supposed to reach the peer over an alternative communication path and call 'drbdadm outdate minor' there" (handler + connectivity, on the surviving Primary, targeting the peer); "DRBD has interfaces that allow an external application to outdate a secondary node as soon as a network interruption occurs" (external app, not autonomous). No kernel mechanism for a node to autonomously outdate its OWN disk purely on connection loss exists.

CONCLUSION: All in-kernel self-outdate (`__outdate_myself`) paths are 2PC/connectivity-gated; quorum loss only suspends/errors I/O without changing disk state; hard-partition cleanup outdates the peer (not self) and only on the Primary. Therefore the minority loser does NOT autonomously self-outdate under a hard partition, and bedrock-d (or a fence-peer/outdate handler) must drive the local outdate — exactly as claimed. Claim's only inaccuracies are a slight line offset and citing 3 of 4 call sites; both errors are immaterial and the uncited 4th site (receiver.c:6961) is likewise 2PC-gated, reinforcing the verdict.

verdicts.claim: RULE_LOST_QUORUM (zero-resync clean path) requires self==peer: drbd_receiver.c:4742 block, :4785-4798 keyed on UUID_FLAG_PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM, reachable only if the loser did NOT rotate (only with Layer-2 outdate or a kernel guard).

Contrast the two GUARDED routes: drbd_sender.c:3443 "if (device->have_quorum[NOW] && drbd_data_accessible(device, NOW)) drbd_uuid_new_current(...)" and drbd_receiver.c:9884-9888 "if (!list_empty(...) && drbd_data_accessible(...) && !test_bit(PRIMARY_LOST_QUORUM, &device->flags) && test_and_clear_bit(NEW_CUR_UUID, ...))" with the explicit comment 9868-9872 "when we lost quorum ... do not create the new UUID immediately!". have_quorum[NEW] is in scope at the unguarded site (used at drbd_state.c:4463 for the quorum-lost khelper) yet the 4466-4471 UUID path omits it. So the 9.2.18 diskless fix does not add a quorum guard to the diskful frozen-Primary paths, matching Bedrock's own analysis in docs/.drbd-study-raw.txt and docs/drbd-uuid-quorum-foundations.md. Hardest refutation attempt (that the ChangeLog wording is loose and the commit also patched diskful paths) fails: the LKML/blog provenance ("bump current uuid when resuming IO with diskless peer", Reisner) and the dedicated diskless-only helper functions confine the fix to the diskless-primary UUID-creation path.
